svg.title: F1 Hospitality Tier Comparison
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-f1-hospitality-tier-comparison; chapter number: 4; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: F1 Hospitality Tier Comparison; subtitle: From a Melbourne Champions Club pass to drive-in Paddock tiers; total range: $600 Champions Club to EUR 25,000 drive-in tiers; caption: Reported price points across F1 premium access, with the Paddock Club sold as a sponsor-funded corporate room first and retail ticket second.; assumptions note: Currencies are mixed as reported (USD and EUR); Pit Stop Lab puts a Paddock Club seat at up to $15,000 per race weekend.; note: Sources: Pit Stop Lab (qjr3BHunOxo @ 00:00:00), Kayvan Goes (2UDtC8EP8GA @ 00:21:38, 00:24:42, 00:30:21), Global Nomads (ePgxCdmE8o8 @ 00:31:34), Live The Dash (emvC24ZLBWo @ 00:12:30).; buckets: label: Melbourne Champions Club; low: 600; high: 600; notes: Entry-level Melbourne hospitality at $600.; label: Melbourne Red Bull Pit Lane; low: 6000; high: 6000; notes: About $6,000 per person bought a run at roughly 40 available seats.; label: Paddock Club ticket; low: 10000; high: 20000; notes: EUR 10,000 to EUR 20,000; about 30% of guests do not pay, and networking scored 1 out of 10 when unassisted.; label: Drive-in tier; low: 25000; high: 25000; notes: EUR 25,000 tier; Kayvan Goes said he would not pay EUR 15,000 and would pay EUR 200 at most.
